story.value: Nobelium is named after Alfred Nobel.
In April 1958, A. Ghiorso, T. Sikkeland, J.R. Walton and G.T. Seaborg clearly discovered and identified nobelium at Berkeley.
Credit for discovering nobelium was given to scientists at the Lawrence Radiation Laboratory, who decided to keep the name nobelium.

uses.value: Only tiny amounts of nobelium have ever been made, so it currently has no uses outside of basic scientific research.
